libs.note: BH-4988 (BH-4975.3). How the planner treats a plan that needs a file an in-flight build claims. bin/plan-overlap.sh exempts collisions on fragment paths (a path the target repo's `## Generated files` table declares, or a fragment directory below and a path under it) and logs `PLAN_HOTSPOT <KEY> choice=build ... fragment-only`. Any other collision defers, and bin/plan-after.sh records `After: <OTHER>`: the free pre-PLAN gate in bin/lib/rb/gates.sh then holds the ticket until OTHER has no claim, no live build dir, no job_claims row and no open PR. The hold is read from the box-local marker file, or, when the box has none (every Fly pool re-offer), from the key's newest overlap_defer job artifact (choice=after); with neither, the ten-minute not-before floor is all that is left. Every choice is one PLAN_HOTSPOT line in the build's pipeline.log and logs/plan-hotspot.log. Both scripts call lib_env_apply plan-hotspot <project>.

knobs.note: Space-separated fragment directories, a trailing / stripped. A bare entry on one side against a path under it on the other, or the bare entry on both sides, is not held. The same FILE inside one on both sides still defers. Read as a settings row, then env, then env/global.env, then this default.

Ceiling on an After: hold, and the window the fleet overlap_defer read looks back over. A marker this old is removed and logged choice=expired, and the ticket goes on to PLAN, where plan-overlap judges it again. 0 = never expire. Read as a settings row, then env, then env/global.env, then 360.
